text.tspan: Tool call: permissions, approval and plan mode
The first decision wins, left to right. Guardrails inside the tools (workspace paths, command rules) always apply, even in bypass mode.
error result returned to the model
result checkpointed, back to the model

g.text: Step 1 of 18 · A tool call arrives
The model asked to run a tool with some arguments.
Step 2 of 18 · pre_tool hook
Hooks run first. They can deny the call or rewrite its arguments.
Step 3 of 18 · Deny rules
Deny rules always win, for example run_command(argv[0]=rm).
Step 4 of 18 · Permission mode
Plan mode refuses anything that is not read-only; bypass and accept_edits pre-approve.
Step 5 of 18 · Ask rules
A matching ask rule pauses for a person to decide.
Step 6 of 18 · Allow rules
A matching allow rule runs the tool without asking.
Step 7 of 18 · Tool risk policy
With no rule matched, high-risk and destructive tools ask; everything else runs.
Step 8 of 18 · Approval requested
This call needs approval, so the run pauses with status AWAITING_INPUT.
Step 9 of 18 · A person decides
From the CLI (approve --allow or --deny) or the HTTP API, optionally with feedback.
Step 10 of 18 · Approved: the tool runs
Validation, timeout, idempotency, and a file snapshot so the edit can be rewound.
Step 11 of 18 · Back to the model
post_tool hook runs and the result is checkpointed.
Step 12 of 18 · Plan mode
A run in plan mode may only read. It explores, then proposes a plan.
Step 13 of 18 · exit_plan
The model submits its plan with the exit_plan tool.
Step 14 of 18 · Plan review
The run pauses so a person can review the plan.
Step 15 of 18 · Rejected with feedback
The feedback goes back to the model.
Step 16 of 18 · Revised plan
The model revises the plan and submits it again.
Step 17 of 18 · Review again
The run pauses for review once more.
Step 18 of 18 · Approved
The mode switches (default or accept_edits) and the run continues with write access.
